description: @ref targets naming an operator keep the operator in the target -- the trailing punctuation stripped from `(see @ref foo)` is part of the name in `@ref Vec::operator[]`. A target that stops at the `operator` keyword names nothing and degrades to a code span.

detail: Subscript {cpp:any}`Vec::operator[]`, equality {cpp:any}`Vec::operator==`, call {cpp:any}`Vec::operator()` and compound {cpp:any}`Vec::operator+=`. In prose (see {cpp:any}`Vec::operator[]`) and at a stop {cpp:any}`Vec::operator+`. A bare {cpp:any}`operator==` resolves too. A conversion operator does not: `Vec::operator` bool stops at the keyword, since the name carries a space and the argument ends there.
